messages.content: Set up a new global application alert configuration with the name 'UrgentAlert77f7', for an error rate threshold of 5%, and send notifications to 'admin@example.com' and 'support@example.com'?

function.name: create_global_application_alert_config
function.description: Create a new global application alert configuration setting for monitoring and notifications. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: A unique name identifying the alert configuration.

alert_type.description: The type of alert to be configured.

threshold.description: The value at which the alert should be triggered. Units depend on the alert_type. This is a float type value.

recipients.description: A list of email addresses to notify when the alert is triggered.

enabled.description: Flag indicating whether the alert configuration is enabled or not.

function.name: enable_global_application_alert_config
function.description: Activate the global alert configuration for an application using the specified identifier. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

id.description: The unique identifier of the application alert configuration to be enabled.

function.name: create_mobile_app_alert_config
function.description: Creates a configuration for mobile app alerts, specifying the conditions and recipients for notifications. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

app_id.description: The unique identifier of the mobile application.

alert_name.description: A descriptive name for the alert.

threshold.description: The numerical value at which the alert should be triggered.

recipients.description: A list of email addresses that will receive the alert.

severity.description: The severity level of the alert.

enabled.description: A flag indicating whether the alert configuration is active.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to set up a new global application alert config. We need to call `create_global_application_alert_config` with appropriate arguments.

We have:

```
{
    name: string,
    alert_type: "error_rate" | "response_time" | "traffic_spike",
    threshold: number,
    recipients: string[],
    enabled?: boolean
}
```

User says: name 'UrgentAlert77f7', alert_type presumably error_rate (since they mention error rate). Threshold 5% -> numeric 0.05? But maybe it's percent as integer 5? They say threshold of 5%. Usually thresholds might be expressed as percentage but we can pass 5. Let's interpret threshold=5. Recipients ['admin@example.com','support@example.com'].

Also optional enabled defaults to true; no need to specify.

Thus we produce JSON payload accordingly.
